ownership_assessment: NO NEW CANONICAL TRUTH OWNER. MVP8 authority/gateway/client scripts compose existing owners only: player ownership and seam handoff stay on the accepted SM1/MVP3 coordinator/carrying/pivot path (cross() untouched); Matter stays on MVP4/MVP7 SharedMatter with MW5 exact-checkpoint restore (restore_exact7 receipt-hash verified); items stay on M4 via service.handle_canonical_item_command executed only on the player's current canonical owner authority; Construction stays on M0/C17 via canonical SeamCommand/DamageRequest/DAMAGE_REPAIR with read-only authority/b replica; recovery stays on MVP7 recovery coordinator + authoritative repository + M6 outbox. The gateway holds orchestration state, counters, bounded evidence, current-state cache and transport coordination only (canonical_state_owned=false asserted in reports). MVP8 checkpoint manifest and restart receipt are composition receipts, not owners. The MVP8 gateway checkpoint file is orchestration evidence; canonical restores always re-derive from the MVP7/MW5/M0/C17 durable stores and cross-check checksums.
boundedness_assessment: STRUCTURALLY ACCEPTABLE. Caps are enforced fail-closed at every round commit (MVP8_BOUNDED_STATE_EXCEEDED aborts the run instead of degrading). Every gateway-to-backend RPC source is a bounded deterministic loop: per-input pre-LOOKUP+route, per-round current-state read + bounds read, per-crossing SM1 export/stage/activate/retire sequence plus a tick barrier of at most 6 LOOKUP samples, DIG probing over a fixed 16-direction candidate set with at most 2 EXECUTE attempts (fail-closed), and idle-only backend liveness of at most one SYNC per backend per 4 s. No unbounded growth loop, no hidden retry, no eviction-for-PASS, no cap or timeout increase exists in the diff. Input observations use the inherited MVP3 bounded ring (<=128) and remain a read-only evidence copy.
backend_rpc_headroom_assessment: THIN BUT STRUCTURALLY SOUND, NOT TIMING-LUCK. Cross-attempt phase1 authority/a sequences: 488 (attempt 1), 498 (attempt 2, headroom 14), 479 (attempt 3 frozen, headroom 33). The observed spread is produced by bounded deterministic variation (DIG probe counts, tick-barrier samples of at most 6, idle-cadence liveness SYNCs), not by a growth loop; the largest observed value already includes the worst observed probing behaviour and remains under cap. The direction of the repairs (current-state cache so client STATUS polls cost zero backend RPCs on hit, validated terminal-snapshot reuse so PHASE_FINISH performs no fresh LOOKUPs, active-traffic liveness skip, compact probe direction set) all reduce traffic structurally rather than shifting it out of band. A cap breach would fail the run closed; it cannot silently invalidate a PASS. Recorded as a non-blocking monitoring observation, not a fix requirement; the cap was not raised.
recovery_staging_assessment: SOUND AND CORRECTLY ORDERED. Phase2 recovery executes staged authenticated RPCs: MVP8_RECOVERY_SETUP bootstraps a fresh epoch-1 read-model decision baseline (fresh Service7 + fresh SharedMatter7 adapters) and then ingests the authenticated current recovered decisions carried by the gateway decision payload; MVP8_RECOVERY_GAMEPLAY restores gameplay/Matter via recover_latest, joins players and hard-fails on MVP8_RECOVERED_OWNERSHIP_EPOCH_MISMATCH against the receipt epochs (checkpoint player ownership epoch + 1), binds live-player gates and rebases the scheduler cursor to the restored canonical server tick (no tick reset); MVP8_RECOVERY_CONSTRUCTION restores M0/C17 from the construction cut with item-graph checksum, cluster export and canonical snapshot equality checks. The epoch-1 baseline exists only as fresh read-model bootstrap; the canonical player ownership epoch is the recovered epoch and is never rolled back; no new decision owner is introduced (each stage returns a compact ack and reuses the existing owners). ENet servicing resumes between stages because the gateway drives stages individually.
seam_and_timing_assessment: SOUND. Seam crossing goes only through the inherited SM1/MVP3 cross() path with byte-for-byte identity/input-watermark preservation, write fencing and replay conflict rejection; no reconnect, teleport, respawn or identity change occurs at an ordinary crossing. After every handoff the gateway waits for an objectively newer canonical server tick on the target (read-only LOOKUPs, at most 6 samples, mutation_performed=false) before allowing further client intents, and the old owner is verified to no longer answer for the actor. Held-input drift is fixed by the mandated directional-MOVE -> ack -> neutral-MOVE -> ack -> round-action client sequence; the neutral fixed-tick tick stops the held intent so CI speed cannot displace the player during long canonical RPCs. There is no client-authoritative displacement and no hidden input retry; the deferred post-activation continuity check requires real displacement plus newer input sequence plus newer state revision on the target.
construction_assessment: SOUND. The historical BASE->ADD->REMOVE build completes in the inherited MVP6 prelude before any MVP8 round. Subsequent BUILD_ADD requires phase REMOVED, consumes the canonical compiled damage_repair_plan, requests ACTION_REPAIR and is applied as canonical_action DAMAGE_REPAIR through the authority/b entry attestation to the authority/a canonical writer; it restores the same salvaged leaf SeamFactory.part_id(100) (asserted) bringing parts to 101. BUILD_REMOVE requires phase ADDED and applies a canonical C9 DamageRequest with SalvagePolicy, severing the leaf bond and returning to 100. No second Construction, no new leaf identity, no completed build-stage replay, no synthetic Construction state; the same construct identity is restored across restart from the cut and verified by canonical snapshot equality and by the acceptance oracle (final collision part count 100).
matter_dig_assessment: SOUND. PREPARE remains a canonical read-only MVP4 query; EXECUTE is sent only with the details of a real accepted PREPARE whose hit is spatially separated from all previously accepted hits (>= 1.0 m, runtime and oracle enforced). Operations use the existing actor-bound operation/mvp4/<actor>/ namespace; a no-effect or MVP4_MATTER_NOT_COMMITTED result never counts as a DIG; execution attempts are capped at 2 per dig with fail-closed behaviour; accepted hit history is carried across the restart inside the restart receipt and reused for separation checks; only the canonical Matter owner mutates store/stream state. No bypass of MVP4_MATTER_NOT_COMMITTED exists.
checkpoint_restart_assessment: SOUND AND CONSERVATIVE. The checkpoint is allowed only at round 8 (next_round=8) after reconnect completion and a canonical normalization transfer of player A back to authority/a that replays the already-acknowledged neutral command without new movement. The cut contains durable rows for both players (ownership_epoch, position, last_input_sequence), gameplay/Matter/Item/Construction checksums, and is sealed with clock=null, held inputs and pending wire cleared, while the process stays alive only for read-only REPORT/SYNC until the gateway acknowledges and sends STOP. The claim is exactly ACKNOWLEDGED QUIESCENT CHECKPOINT RESTART; arbitrary uncheckpointed power-loss recovery is explicitly not claimed.
matter_resync_assessment: SOUND. After restart the fresh SharedMatter instance does not assume peers connected. Each fresh client performs an explicit MVP8_MATTER_CONNECT which reads the canonical owner's current stream_sequence/state_hash and registers CURRENT state via MVP4_CONNECT with a sync request; unexpected queued frames fail the resync; no mutation, no old-frame replay, no second terrain truth, no unexpected backlog. Gateway and both resume clients report matter_resynced a=true b=true in the frozen artifact.
backend_liveness_assessment: SOUND. BackendLink continues to service its own ENet events (idle frame servicing plus sibling servicing during synchronous RPC waits), real backend disconnect remains fatal (MVP3_BACKEND_DISCONNECTED, reconnect forbidden), read-only SYNC is issued only when the authenticated sequence did not move during the interval (useful traffic itself counts as liveness evidence), no backend reconnect is performed, and the diff changes no timeout policy.
negative_controls_assessment: VERIFIED 14/14. Each of the 14 mutants was read against the acceptance oracle and independently confirmed rejected in the frozen attempt-3 manifest: skip_reconnect, reuse_same_peer, wrong_restart_round, missing_round, missing_postrestart_motion, queue_overflow, duplicate_item_identity, terminal_overflow, missing_collision, lost_build_cycle, missing_dig_hit, missing_matter_resync, overlapping_dig_hit, missing_checkpoint_player. All are genuine false-positive mutations (each breaks at least one real invariant), not strawmen.

findings.problem: Phase1 authority/a backend RPC sequence reached 498 against the fixed cap 512 in attempt 2 (headroom 14).
findings.why_not_blocking: All traffic sources are bounded deterministic loops and the cap fails closed; the frozen attempt 3 measured 479. Availability risk only, no correctness or masking risk, and no eviction/retry/cap increase exists.
findings.required_fix: None required. Monitor phase1 authority/a sequence on future exact reruns; do not raise the cap.

findings.problem: The negative-control oracle check_pack re-implements a subset of the positive invariants instead of reusing evidence_checks, so the two oracles can drift.
findings.why_not_blocking: All 14 mutants were verified to break a real invariant, and the positive checks independently assert the same properties on the live evidence.
findings.required_fix: Optional future refactor to derive the mutation oracle from evidence_checks.

findings.problem: The checkpoint-return transfer runs with prove_post_input=false, so the MVP3 deferred continuity marker for player A can remain open in gateway orchestration evidence at checkpoint time.
findings.why_not_blocking: The marker is gateway-side carrying evidence, not a pending canonical mutation; native owners are verified quiescent for the cut (sealed clock, cleared held input, sealed Service7 cut), and the checkpoint stores durable player rows directly.
